runbooks.name: article_playbook
runbooks.description: Article Playbook — give the agent a link, get a filtered, tiered view of someone else's article: quotes, themes, ELI5, synthesis, similar-to. Second runbook-as-data instance (spec/article-playbook-v0.1.md in a2ui-private), sibling to learning_hub. Unlike learning_hub, this runbook's whole reason for existing is that every lens except `quotes` is a distortion of the source by construction — the composition below exists to keep that distortion visible (epistemic tiers ARE hub subject tabs, colored distinctly) and checkable (evidence spans verified as verbatim substrings of `source_excerpt`), not just to lay out tabs.

input_contract.title: string (required) — article title
input_contract.source: object (required) — {url (required), author?, published?, read_minutes?, retrieved: boolean (required, true only if the agent actually fetched url in this session)}. Rendered in the hub header, not inside a lens — it must stay on screen regardless of which lens tab is active.
input_contract.source_excerpt: string (REQUIRED, ~8KB cap). Verbatim passages the agent actually drew its claims from — not the whole article. A payload without it is REFUSED, not degraded: evidence spans are only meaningful if they can be checked against something, and this is the only thing they can be checked against (spec mitigation 2). Copy this same string into the `source_excerpt` field of every interpreted-tier lens block (themes, eli5, synthesis, freeform) — the renderer verifies each lens's evidence locally, one atom block at a time, so it needs its own copy rather than shared page-level context.
input_contract.lenses: array (required, non-empty). Each entry is {id, tier}, where id selects a key from composition.slide_kind_atoms and tier is one of extracted|interpreted|external — must match composition.lens_tier for that id, except freeform, whose tier is genuinely caller-chosen. Each present tier becomes one hub subject tab (composition.tier_subjects); a tier with no present lens gets no tab. `quotes` is effectively mandatory: if omitted, the engine still renders a source-only tab from `source` rather than dropping the reader's exit into the original text. A lens outside the caller's chosen template (composition.templates) is marked off-template in the UI.

content_by_lens.themes: source_excerpt (copy of the payload-level field); items: array of {label, evidence, weight?}. evidence is REQUIRED per item and MUST be a verbatim substring of source_excerpt — an item that fails the check renders with an "unverified" marker, never silently.
content_by_lens.eli5: source_excerpt (copy); text (the simplified rewrite — hedges in the original, e.g. "may", "some evidence suggests", MUST survive into text rather than be compressed out); evidence: array of verbatim substrings of source_excerpt the rewrite draws from.
content_by_lens.synthesis: source_excerpt (copy); points: array of {point, evidence}, same per-item verbatim-evidence requirement as themes.
content_by_lens.similar: items: array of {title, why, url?, retrieved?}; verified: true only if every item's url was actually retrieved this session. If verified is false (or omitted), the lens renders in the EXTERNAL tab labelled "suggestions, unverified" rather than as a bibliography. Never render an unretrieved title as if it were a citation — if neither condition (verified, or per-item retrieved) holds for an item, omit that item rather than fabricate a bibliography entry.
content_by_lens.context: items: array of {label, note, url?, retrieved?} — same retrieval-honesty rule as similar.
content_by_lens.freeform: source_excerpt (copy, if tier is extracted/interpreted); label (agent-chosen, e.g. "Regulatory impact"); tier; text; evidence (array, required in practice for extracted/interpreted tiers — external-tier freeform is unverified by definition and may omit it); off_template defaults true. Use this ONLY for a lens kind the catalogue lacks — a lens kind that already exists above must be selected, not reinvented here (spec: "inventing a lens kind — NO").

runbooks.parsing_guide:
Consumers (the calling agent) fetch the article with their own tooling, read it, and fill this contract; composition is the runbook's job, filling it honestly is the consumer's. Six mitigations this runbook exists to enforce, from spec/article-playbook-v0.1.md (a2ui-private):
1. Epistemic status must be visible per lens, not implied — hence tier_subjects above: each tier is its own hub subject tab, colored distinctly; never render two different tiers under the same tab or chrome.
2. Every interpreted claim (themes item, synthesis point, eli5 rewrite, interpreted-tier freeform) carries a verbatim `evidence` span that is checked against `source_excerpt`, not merely present. Missing evidence renders an explicit "no supporting quote" marker rather than being dropped; evidence not found verbatim in source_excerpt renders "unverified" rather than being trusted. This is the single highest-value check in the whole runbook — test it with a deliberately fabricated quote before trusting a payload.
3. `quotes` is the one lens that is never truly optional — the reader's exit into the author's own words must always be one click away. If a caller's content omits it, compose a source-only quotes tab (title + link from `source`) rather than drop the tab.
4. Source url/author/date live in the hub header (hub_header_from: source), never inside a lens — a view of someone's article that doesn't show whose article it is has already failed.
5. `similar` is the dangerous lens: a model will confidently invent plausible articles it never read. Render it as a real citation list only when `verified` is true; otherwise (the default) label it "suggestions, unverified" within its EXTERNAL tab and never let an unretrieved title read as if it were sourced.
6. No lens may exceed the source's own confidence. Hedges in the original ("may", "some evidence suggests", "the author argues") are load-bearing, not noise — dropping them during eli5/synthesis is the most common way a faithful-looking summary becomes false.
Template selection: default to composition.templates.critical (quotes + themes + synthesis) unless the caller names quick or research. A lens outside the chosen template is composed anyway if requested, but marked off-template in the rendered UI — "the model added a lens" must stay visually distinguishable from "this is the standard view".
Pagination: same per-page ~8100 char ceiling and automatic subject-level split as learning_hub (see runbooks/learning_hub.yaml's parsing_guide and spec/nav-budget-pagination-v0.1.md, a2ui-private) — payload size here is normally a non-issue (five lenses of a few hundred words is 2-4 KB), so splitting is expected to be rare in practice.

runbooks.name: learning_hub
runbooks.description: Learning Hub — a curriculum/revision study app: subject tabs across the top, slide pills per subject, each slide one learning interaction (timeline, drill, flashcards, quiz, takeaways, or method steps). First runbook-as-data instance (spec/runbook-pattern-v0.1.md in a2ui-private): the composition block below is the authored bill of materials; consumers shape content to the input_contract (see parsing_guide) and stamp via the MCP emit_runbook_surface tool. Judgment lives here, spent once — callers supply content only and cannot compose badly.

input_contract.title: string (required) — app title
input_contract.subjects: array (required) of {label, color?, slides}. label may carry an emoji prefix ("📐 Maths"); color is the subject's hex accent.
input_contract.slides: each slide = {label, kind, hero?, ...content fields by kind}. label is the pill text (short, emoji prefix welcome). hero (optional) = {heading, subtext?, badge?} — rendered as a banner above the slide content.

content_by_kind.drill: questions: array of {question, answer}; duration?: seconds (default 1200)
content_by_kind.flashcards: cards: array of {front, back}; label_front?; label_back?; accent?
content_by_kind.quiz: question: string; options: array of strings; correct: 0-based index; explanation: string

runbooks.parsing_guide:
Consumers shape their source into the input_contract; parsing is the consumer's documented job, composition is the runbook's. From a knowledge-catalogue curriculum.md (typed-section grammar, knowledge-catalogue/SPEC.md): {#timeline} sections -> kind timeline ("### YYYY | Title" lines become events); {#drill} -> kind drill; {#concept}/{#glossary} -> kind flashcards; [!PIÈGE] callouts -> kind quiz; {#key_takeaways} -> kind takeaways; {#method} -> kind method. One subject per curriculum domain, slide labels short. All content field shapes are renderer-ground-truth (extracted from the live brevet app's payload).
Pagination: the per-page size ceiling (~8100 chars) is enforced per subject, not per whole hub. If all subjects fit one page, the engine returns a single hub-as-one-page url (subject tabs + slide pills, all navigation client-side). If not, it automatically splits by subject, seeds each subject's own hub-as-one-page url server-side, and returns one hub-of-pages nav page linking them by short ?nav= reference (name overhead only, no embedded content — so total curriculum size has no real ceiling). Response carries `pages[]` + `seeded: true` when this happened. No consumer action needed either way; the returned url is ready to use as-is. See spec/nav-budget-pagination-v0.1.md (a2ui-private) for the design.
